column1: # page-roster 1
# The gate's page coverage record (#1382). One row per page view; hand-edited, and
# NOT generated by tool/overflow_baseline.sh — nothing here is a sweep output.
# rule a file named *_view.dart directly inside a views/ directory, at any depth under lib/page/
# dispositions swept | queued | excluded:<reason>
# ms_per_cell measured milliseconds per cell of this page's 9 widths x 26 locales; `-` means NOT MEASURED
# fixture_debt a `-` on a queued row is #1370's finding that no fixture gets that view past its loader yet
# basis section 11.2's: an isolated --plain-name run, its coordinate tests only, over one page's cells
# basis-note Figures were taken while a page was 8 widths x 26 locales = 208 cells until #1372 made
# basis-note it 9 x 26 = 234 on 2026-08-26. That change did NOT invalidate the column: a per-cell rate
# basis-note is the quantity that survives a width being added, and the widest cells are the cheapest
# basis-note to lay out. Every figure here is now on the same reading: --plain-name, --reporter json
# basis-note per-test durations summed and divided by cells, three runs, median committed. #1377
# basis-note established the durations basis over wall-clock-minus-control (a ~6s startup with ~1s of
# basis-note variance has a wider error band than the drift being measured); #1378 added the
# basis-note three-runs-median rule after four passes over pnp_entry read 21.2, 18.5, 11.6 and 10.9.
# basis-note WHAT #1380 RE-MEASURED, and what it did not. All 21 of this wave's pages were measured
# basis-note here, three runs each. Seven of them entered the roster in this wave's first slice still
# basis-note carrying #1370's one-shot wall-clock figures, and re-reading them on this basis moved
# basis-note five by far more than #1377's +/-7% floor: support -63.2% (41.0 -> 15.1),
# basis-note firmware_update -58.2% (46.4 -> 19.4), ai_assistant/router_assistant -32.3% (31.9 -> 21.6),
# basis-note advanced_settings -19.5% (16.9 -> 13.6), unified_diagnostics -14.6% (17.8 -> 15.2). Two
# basis-note agreed: test_console +1.5% (53.4 -> 54.2) and remote_assistance +0.8% (13.3 -> 13.4).
# basis-note Every drift is DOWNWARD except those two, and support's -63% took no lib fix at all, so
# basis-note this is the basis and not the fixes. Note also that the two that agreed are one cheap
# basis-note page and one expensive one, so the disagreement is not simply the sub-20ms band the
# basis-note note below warns about. The 22 pages from the pilot and waves 1-3 were NOT re-measured
# basis-note by #1380: their figures are already three-run medians on this basis, taken 2026-08-25/26,
# basis-note and re-running 22 pages to re-confirm a two-day-old reading buys less than it costs. So
# basis-note the distribution below mixes measurement DATES, not bases.
# basis-note Read any figure under ~20ms/cell as +/-40% and re-measure before planning against one:
# basis-note only 1 of #1378's 7 comparable pages landed inside the +/-7% floor and the rest moved
# basis-note -70% to +63%. Two causes seen so far, neither of them noise: a fixture difference
# basis-note (pnp_static_ip +63%, 36.5 -> 59.6, because this wave's state expands the DNS rows, so
# basis-note five IPv4 fields render where #1370's default state rendered three) and an error path
# basis-note (usp_menu_view -42.6%, 40.1 -> 23.0, because #1370 measured it with no overrides, where
# basis-note lanDataProvider and uspInstantPrivacyProvider both land in AsyncError and a throw, a
# basis-note stack capture and a log line are charged to all 234 cells). The rule that falls out, and
# basis-note the one #1380 was opened on: a queued figure taken WITHOUT a fixture is not a prediction
# basis-note of the swept figure, and where it differs it reads HIGH. It is an upper bound. Confirmed
# basis-note by this wave on the 13 rows that had one - not one came in above its queued figure.
# basis-note auto_parent_first_login_view's 19.9 is a FIRST measurement, not a drift: it was #1370's
# basis-note one unmeasurable row (its `-` meant no fixture got the view past its opening state).
# basis-note WHAT A FIGURE IN THIS COLUMN IS NOT: it is not the page's share of the sweep file's wall
# basis-note clock. Every figure here is measured with that page's suite run alone. #1380 also ran the
# basis-note whole 43-page file under --reporter json and divided each page's group by 234, and the
# basis-note two columns disagree per page in BOTH directions: 30 of 43 pages are CHEAPER in company
# basis-note (ratios 0.45-0.98, median 0.70), 4 are mildly dearer (1.12-1.38), and 9 are severely
# basis-note dearer - firmware_update 4.47 (19.4 -> 86.7), local_network 3.99 (104.7 -> 417.7),
# basis-note test_console 3.25, sliver_dashboard 3.04, dmz 2.69, login_local 2.60, usp_dashboard 2.45,
# basis-note pnp_static_ip 2.18, local_reset_router_password 1.80. It is not position in the run
# basis-note (Pearson 0.29; the offenders sit at positions 12-40) and it is not harness overhead
# basis-note (only 1.0s of the run's 531.2s is outside a test body). Why those nine and not the other
# basis-note 34 is unexplained, and #1380 did not explain it. Two consequences for anyone reading this
# basis-note column: (1) it is a reproducible per-page MEASUREMENT and stays the basis for comparing
# basis-note pages to each other; (2) any sum of it is a FLOOR on the file's cost, never an estimate -
# basis-note the sum below reads 278.0s where the file measures 553s. Do not balance shards on it.
# distribution FINAL, all 43 swept pages, 2026-08-27 (#1380). n=43, so the median is an element and
# distribution not a mean of two: 21.5 (usp_apps_view). min 11.0 (home), max 104.7 (local_network),
# distribution mean 27.6, sum 1188.2 ms/cell => 43 x 234 = 10,062 cells = 278.0s of pump time.
# distribution Right-skewed, which is the shape that matters for #1371 and #1380 both: mean > median
# distribution by 28%, and the five most expensive pages (104.7, 63.5, 59.6, 58.6, 54.2) are 28.7% of
# distribution the total while being 11.6% of the pages. 28 of 43 pages are under the mean, 20 of 43
# distribution are under 20ms/cell, and only 8 are over 40. Quartiles 15.1 / 21.5 / 33.4.
# distribution This replaces every projection published before it. #1379 projected 43 pages at 321.3s
# distribution from a 22.4 median; summed from real figures it is 278.0s, so that projection over-read
# distribution by 13.5% - in the same direction and for the same reason as the queued column above.
# distribution But 278.0s is a floor and not the file's cost. Same-run json, same 43 pages: the 430
# distribution page tests sum to 450.6s, 1.62x this figure, and the whole file measures 553s (median of
# distribution 533.93 / 558.25 / 615.16) once its 18 readability tests (75.2s) and its `loading` test
# distribution are in. See the basis-note above for the per-page in-situ ratios, and read 278.0s as
# distribution "the pump time these pages own", not as "what the sweep costs the gate".
# distribution Take it with statistics.median over this file's non-`-` rows; re-derive anything
# distribution downstream of it in one pass rather than editing the number in place.
# verdict The four exclusion candidates #1380 inherited. ALL FOUR STAY IN. An exclusion is a row with
# verdict a reason, and unreachability is the only reason this epic accepts; none of the four is
# verdict unreachable. Written out because three of them were argued on something else.
# verdict 1. usp_sliver_dashboard_view - #1370's verdict stands: non-routed but constructed at
# verdict usp_dashboard_view.dart:64, and routed vs reachable are different questions. Its cost
# verdict objection is now gone too: #1370 read 315.4ms/cell and called it the epic's most expensive
# verdict page by 6x; three runs on this basis read 58.6, so it is the 4th most expensive and 4.9%
# verdict of the sweep. Nothing had to absorb 66s of pump CPU, and no #1371 re-open was needed.
# verdict 2. usp_dashboard_view - the open question was whether a page-level probe measures anything
# verdict the chrome and card sweeps do not. Answered on coordinates, as the AC required, not by
# verdict assertion. (a) COVERAGE: kPageSweepWidths is {320,480,601,905,1080,1241,1280,1441,1681} and
# verdict kChromeSweepWidths is {320,375,480,600,601,640,700,768,800,905,1024,1280}; the intersection
# verdict is 5 widths, so 1080, 1241, 1441 and 1681 - four of this page's nine, including the #1302
# verdict desktop pinch at 1241 - are visited by no chrome cell in any locale. (b) TREE: at the five
# verdict shared widths the chrome sweep pumps ChromeTopBarFamily / ChromeHeaderFamily, i.e. the bar
# verdict and the header alone. Neither contains the grid or a single card, so a shared width is not
# verdict a shared measurement. Its one citation of this file, page_chrome_family.dart:289, quotes
# verdict usp_dashboard_view.dart:36 to explain why the header is a sibling of the content - which is
# verdict an argument that the content is NOT in its tree. (c) AXIS: the card sweep's axis is card
# verdict width at a computed grid realization, not screen width, so its cells are not coordinates in
# verdict this space at all; it never renders a page. What the sweep found is nothing: this page is at
# verdict zero across 234 cells today, so the verdict rests on coverage of coordinates and not on a
# verdict find. It costs 63.5ms/cell, the 2nd most expensive page in the roster.
# verdict 3. usp_test_console_view - a developer surface, and the AC asked what an exclusion costs.
# verdict Reachability first, because it decides the question: route_usp_dashboard.dart:201 registers
# verdict it under `if (kDebugMode || GlobalConfig.feature.enableTestConsole)`, and enableTestConsole
# verdict defaults to false (build_config.dart:54, --dart-define=test_console). So it is absent from a
# verdict default release build but present in EVERY debug build and in any build made with that
# verdict define, which is how it is reached in practice. "Not reachable" is therefore false as
# verdict stated, and it stays. What excluding it would have cost, stated as the AC asked: the single
# verdict largest find in the epic - 52 cells over at usp_test_console_view.dart:1147, worst +109px,
# verdict and the ONLY page of all 45 that breaks in `en` rather than needing a long locale. That is a
# verdict defect every engineer and every QA build hits at 320px in English. Which way it cuts: the
# verdict page is 54.2ms/cell, 4.6% of the sweep, so the trade on offer was the epic's biggest find
# verdict for 4.6% of its runtime. Kept and fixed to zero.
# verdict 4. router_assistant_view - the AC's question was conditional on it being feature-gated off
# verdict in shipping configurations, and it is not: route_usp_dashboard.dart:225 registers it
# verdict unconditionally, with no kDebugMode and no flag. It ships, so the test_console reasoning
# verdict does not even need to be reached. Its 7 cells at :409 +89px were user-visible defects.
# verdict Kept and fixed to zero.
# unblocked pnp_setup_view was the one row this register has carried as measured-but-queued, and it is
# unblocked kept here because the distinction is the useful part: it was never fixture debt.
# unblocked pnpWizardConfiguringState in test/mocks/test_data/scenes/pnp_scene_data.dart got it past its
# unblocked loader on the first attempt and #1378 measured all 208 cells through it — 208 of 208 red at
# unblocked +12.0px on this page's 3-step wizard, on ui_kit v2.40.1's AppStepper bar variant, which
# unblocked divided constraints.maxWidth while AppFocusIndicator padded each bar by ringOffset=2.0
# unblocked unconditionally. Section 8's graduation rule is what kept it out: a whole page of debt does
# unblocked not enter the gate, and the only fixture that laid out clean was a 1-step wizard, i.e. one
# unblocked rendering no AppStepper. Filed as linksys/privacyGUI-UI-kit#70, fixed there by 936c1da6 and
# unblocked released as v2.40.2 on 2026-08-26; the tripwire in
# unblocked test/page/instant_setup/views/pnp_setup_view_test.dart went red with an empty incident list
# unblocked on the bump, which is the signal it was written to give, and was then deleted. Swept the
# unblocked same day, so this row's disposition is the shorter half of its story.
